xterm256.distance: sum of squared 8-bit RGB channel deltas; lower index wins a tie
xterm256.rule: nearest entry that keeps the token floor against every 256-colour surface that token may use

status.label: Queued
status.meaning: Waiting for a Worker to claim the Ticket

closePalette.effect: clear the query and restore the opener

keyboard.listMotionWhen: the focused surface is the result list, another list, or the transcript, or palette navigation mode is on
keyboard.typing: j and k insert text while the palette query or any other text field has the caret, including when the query is empty. Navigation mode is the only time they do not.

navigationMode.effect: j and k move the highlight and are not inserted
navigationMode.leaveOnPrintable: any other printable character turns navigation mode off and is inserted into the query
navigationMode.web: keydown when Alt is the only modifier and code is KeyN; preventDefault so an Option character is not inserted
navigationMode.reserved: ctrl+n is not a binding. Browsers keep it for a new window. This model does not use fullscreen or the Keyboard Lock API.
navigationMode.fallback: When alt+n is not delivered, navigation mode stays off. Up and Down still move the highlight in the query. ctrl+down still focuses the result list, where j and k move.

focusResultList.ownsChord: the open palette handles ctrl+down on the web

focusQuery.fromResultList: j and k move the highlight on the result list. Any other printable character returns focus to the query and inserts that character

keyboard.tabInPalette: accept the highlighted completion; never leaves the palette

previousFocus.effect: move to the previous stop in the focus order
previousFocus.inPalette: inert: does nothing, focus stays in the palette trap
previousFocus.neverOverridden: browsers need shift+tab for reverse tab order (accessibility); no surface rebinds it
previousFocus.changedFrom: the shipped TUI bound shift+tab (s-tab) to cycle mode auto, dispatch, read-only; that binding moves to alt+m

modeCycle.effect: cycle to the next mode, wrapping after read-only
modeCycle.web: keydown when Alt is the only modifier and code is KeyM; preventDefault so an Option character is not inserted (same handling as alt+n)

keys.when: on the web always; in the TUI when the terminal reports it (kitty CSI 13;2u, xterm CSI 27;2;13~)
escape then enter within 0.1 s (escape flushes after 0.1 s)

permission.typing: a, s and d answer the prompt and are not inserted into the composer

palette.commandToken: case-insensitive subsequence of the canonical name, the slash name without the slash, or an alias with one leading slash stripped. Characters appear in order and need not be contiguous, so dsp and DSP match dispatch.

fuzzy.fold: lowercase (Unicode casefold) of needle and haystack
haystacks: slash name without the leading slash
alias with one leading slash stripped
fuzzy.alignment: greedy left to right, taking the leftmost later character
fuzzy.gapCost: endIndex - startIndex - (needleLength - 1); a contiguous run is 0
fuzzy.needle: the query with one leading slash removed, then folded
fuzzy.bestHaystack: each command is ranked by its best haystack
surfaces: tui / at composer column 0 (opens the palette prefilled with /)

palette.matchOrder: fuzzy rank, then canonical name. An empty query stays in idleOrder
palette.argumentCompletion: after the command token and a space; unique prefix of an id or name, case-sensitive for hex ids as in _matched_target; never fuzzy

accept.tab: accept the highlighted token and add a trailing space when the form still needs an argument; never leaves the palette
accept.enter: run a complete form; on an incomplete form insert the highlighted argument instead, or show the error hint when none is offered

precedence: full Ticket UUID, returned as written
in-range 1-based index into the last painted list
unique case-sensitive prefix of a known Ticket id
target.index: #N or a bare integer N, 1-based, into _snapshot_ids (the numbered snapshot, or the first three recent Tickets when the snapshot is empty). An in-range index wins over a prefix. int() parses the digits, so 00000001 is index 1 when the list has a first row.
target.uuid: full Ticket UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex), returned as written
target.prefix: token matching [0-9a-fA-F-]{8,} with at least 8 hex digits, when exactly one known Ticket id startswith the token (case-sensitive)
target.knownIds: snapshot ids, then recent Tickets and jobs, then the current Ticket, first copy kept
target.outOfRangeIndex: A bare integer past the painted list falls through to prefix matching. 12345678 resolves when exactly one known Ticket id starts with 12345678, including an id that is only on the jobs list. A leading # does not fall through.
target.noMatch: not a target. _resolve_target raises no job at index when the token is #N or all digits, and returns any other unresolved token unchanged
target.ambiguous: two or more prefix matches raise '{token} matches more than one job: {ids}' with the ids joined by commas; completion lists the matches and inserts nothing
target.completionOrder: list index, then known ids in the knownIds order

shippedSlashCompleter.rule: case-sensitive prefix of the name with the slash removed, only while the line has no space, sorted by command name, at most 60 rows

strings.rule: Status labels, command names, key hints and error hints are never truncated or ellipsised. Measure in terminal cells: a CJK (East Asian Wide or Fullwidth) character is 2 cells, everything else 1. A column sized for a label fits the widest label of both locales; free text (titles, prose) may wrap or truncate, labels may not.
